children: JFrog’s revenue rose 31% year over year in the third quarter, as growth from existing customers and new customers lifted subscription sales. The company swung to net income from a year-earlier loss, supported by higher gross margin and interest income, while operating expenses increased.
¹ Reported as “Total subscription revenue”. ² Reported as “Net income (loss)”. ³ Reported as “Net income (loss) per share, diluted”.
: About $35.1M of quarterly subscription revenue growth came from existing customers, with the remainder from new customers.
: SaaS subscriptions accounted for 57% of revenue, compared with 46% in the prior-year quarter.
: 1,357 customers had ARR of $100,000 or more as of September 30, 2026, up from 1,168 as of December 31, 2025.
: Net dollar retention was 124% as of September 30, 2026, compared with 118% a year earlier.
: Gross margin increased to 80% from 77%, driven by revenue growth, improved operating leverage and lower intangible amortization, partly offset by higher hosting costs.
